transport: Not applicable — these are transport, not protocol. MK2.2b presents RS232; MK2-USB and MK3-USB present USB-serial; both speak the MK2/MK3 protocol at 2400 8N1 (see victron-vebus-mk2). The VE.Bus Smart dongle presents BLE advertisements (see victron-ble-instant-readout-vebus). DMC is a VE.Bus remote panel with no third-party interface.

gotchas: A Digital Multi Control on the bus disables remote control of mode and input current limit. The GX register list says so against registers 22 and 33 ("See Venus-OS manual for limitations, for example when VE.Bus BMS or DMC is installed"), and the MK2 MasterMultiLED frame carries a "DMC dedicated" bit whose meaning is "

One interface per VE.Bus SYSTEM, not per unit. Vendor FAQ Q1: "Do I need an MK2 or MK3 for each product in a system with multiple VE.Bus products in parallel or three-phase? No. Per VE.Bus system you need only one of those interfaces."

There is no RS232 version of the MK3: "The Victron interface MK3-USB also has a built-in RS232 to USB Converter. There is no RS232 version of the MK3 available." And there is no protocol difference between MK2 and MK3 — "Note that there is no difference in protocol between the MK2 and MK3 interfaces." Only firmware-gat

The USB-serial chipset inside the MK3-USB is not stated in any vendor document found. That is a live risk, not a footnote: docs/HARDWARE.md already rejected the EPEver CC-USB-RS485-150U because its Exar XR21B1411 has no mainline Linux driver. Plug one into the Pi and read dmesg — bench question, unanswered.

The MK2/MK3 firmware is updated only by connecting it to a PC running VEConfigure3 and making a connection to a Multi. There is no Linux path documented. A Multi too new for the interface's firmware is a plausible first-day failure with no in-place fix.
